title: Northfield high-rise rezoning and McCormick centre construction award
subtitle: Accessibility design standards, heritage designations, RIM Park refrigeration upgrades, respectful behaviour policy and the 2027 council schedule
overview: Council approved Official Plan Amendment 56 and Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-08 for the Northfield Drive West and Weber Street North lands {{vote:m12}}. The site can now accommodate 11 residential towers, a possible school site, parks and light employment uses. The plan is long-term, and a master plan for parks, a school-site holding provision and transportation studies still have to be completed. One councillor declared a conflict and did not take part.

Council awarded the construction contract for Phase B of the Albert McCormick Community Centre and McCormick library expansion to S.G. Cunningham (Kitchener) Limited, and released the related capital funding {{vote:m9}}. It also approved new Facility Accessibility Design Standards {{vote:m6}}, a $2.73 million refrigeration upgrade at the RIM Park Sportsplex {{vote:m7}}, and a replacement Respectful Behaviour Policy {{vote:m8}}.

On heritage, council issued a notice of intention to designate 131 William Street West {{vote:m10}} and designated five downtown properties {{vote:m11}}. A delegate also asked for a review of the food vehicle rules in the Business Licensing By-law; the minutes record no motion on this, but the mayor said staff would be asked to look at it. Council also approved the 2027 meeting schedule {{vote:m5}}.

decisions.item: Northfield official plan and zoning amendments
decisions.detail: Council approved OPA 56 and Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-08 for 170-200 Northfield Drive West and 570-655 Weber Street North with three wording changes, including a 15.0 metre rail setback in place of 18.0 metres.

decisions.item: AMCC and McCormick library Phase B award
decisions.detail: Council awarded the Phase B renovation and expansion contract to S.G. Cunningham (Kitchener) Limited for a total of $13,211,174.94 and released $9,696,000 in capital funding, with $4,039,000 in development charge funding to be released on January 1, 2027.
Council approved the standards for city facilities and delegated minor updates to the Commissioner of Community Services.
Council awarded the tender to CIMCO Refrigeration for a total of $2,729,096.35 including unrecoverable HST.
Council approved a new Respectful Behaviour Policy A-009 that repeals and replaces the 2014 version.
Council approved designating five downtown properties, including the Letter Block, Conrad Block, Waterloo Theatre, Roos Building and Boehm House, under the Ontario Heritage Act.
Council directed the Clerk to issue a Notice of Intention to Designate 131 William Street West as a heritage property.
Council named staff owner representatives and alternates for the drinking water, stormwater and wastewater systems.

debate: On the Northfield application, one councillor worried about fitting logistics, a school and dense housing on one car-dependent site. They asked how pedestrian safety and travel by other modes would be handled. Staff said warehousing would be small scale, and that a broader transportation study and later site-specific studies would follow.

Staff explained that parks staff prefer public parkland over privately owned public space, and that the final park size and layout would be settled at site plan through a holding provision. The applicant's planner said the plan is long-term and may change, for example if the school board buys the school site, and that the market will decide what is built first.

Councillors supporting the Northfield plan pointed to the changes since the 2024 informal meeting: fewer towers, lower maximum height, a larger park area and a school site. One councillor noted the area will become busier for traffic.

On the accessibility standards, councillors asked how the document would be updated. Staff said it would be formally reviewed every four years, with lessons from projects tracked internally in the meantime. Staff and a delegate from the accessibility advisory committee stressed that consistent design across spaces matters and that no single design suits everyone.

A delegate asked for the Business Licensing By-law's food vehicle exception to be clarified. They said it does not define "guest", does not address online orders, and does not cover someone who owns, lives at and runs a business from the same property. Council asked no questions, and the mayor said staff would review the by-law without promising any outcome.
